summary: Round 2 of 2 on tier2-webhook plan v2 (scale: feature, design-only, 1 milestone, 5 steps). All three round-1 blockers are cleared and nothing that passed in round 1 regressed, so the outcome is verified: executability pass, grounding pass, testability pass, 0 blockers, 9 warnings. PV-001 is closed by a Case.Tier2_Notified_At__c field permission on Tier2_Webhook_Admin, with A14's claim about the checker's object-row rule confirmed in that checker's source rather than taken on trust, A13 covering the scheduling user, and the manual test carrying the absence check no checker can make. PV-002 is closed by citing apex/apex-hardcoded-id-elimination and binding its Example-3 Group-by-DeveloperName shape into inputs.detection verbatim. PV-003 is closed by a third M1-S04 checker that this verifier probed itself: check_error_handling_framework.py exits 1 on an empty directory with the exact message the plan quotes, so every step now carries a test with failure power over an absent artefact. Four round-1 warnings are folded in as well: the ten branch quotes are now character-for-character verbatim, M1-S01 names the elements its flagless checker requires, the UNVERIFIED AuthHeader grammar is manual deploy step 1, and the test classes carry the publish-result and deliver() rules.
confidence_rationale: HIGH per the plan-verifier rubric: all three lenses ran on all five steps plus the milestone and the cross-step set, in a full re-run rather than a diff; every verdict carries evidence naming the file read or the command run and what it printed; and each of the three cleared blockers was re-checked against the artefact of record rather than against the planner's description of it - the field permission against the checker's own source, the queue lookup against the skill's fenced Example 3, and the new checker against its own --help, an empty directory and a missing one. The two judgement calls made against the letter of a lens row (M1-S04's org-only manual clause, and treating the deploy-order prose lag as a warning) are both recorded with their reasoning.

findings.title: CLEARED — Case.Tier2_Notified_At__c FLS is now granted, and the grant is checker-safe
findings.detail: v2's Tier2_Webhook_Admin declares the field readable and editable, with the reason stated in the input itself. The shape is safe against the checker that reads it: check_field_permissions() guards its object-row rule with 'if has_object_row and owner not in granted_objects', so a field permission on Case with no Case objectPermissions row cannot fire it - which is what A14 claims, verified in source rather than on the fixture. D14 is restated as the union of escalating users and the scheduling user, A13 carries the scheduling half with the cited skill's 'for scheduled jobs the scheduler' quote behind it, and because no checker in the library fails on a grant that was never written, the M1-S02 manual test now reads the entry by name and says so.

findings.title: CLEARED — the queue lookup is cited, bound and quoted from the skill's worked example
findings.detail: M1-S03 now cites apex/apex-hardcoded-id-elimination and inputs.detection names the exact shape: a private static Map<String, Id> filled once per transaction from SELECT Id, DeveloperName FROM Group WHERE Type = 'Queue', read through a queueId(String devName) accessor. That is Example 3's 'After' block element for element, so 'one SOQL per transaction' is the shape's own property rather than an assertion the plan added, and the step states outright that a hardcoded Group Id is not the fallback because apex-builder's REFUSAL_SECURITY_GUARD (d) refuses it. The ban reaches the tests too.

findings.detail: The step declares check_error_handling_framework.py --manifest-dir artefacts/M1-S04, whose skill was already in its skills[]. Probed independently: the script exists, --help shows --manifest-dir, an empty directory gives exit 1 with 'ISSUE: No .cls or .trigger files found under <dir> — confirm --manifest-dir points to a Salesforce metadata source directory' (the message the plan quotes), and a missing directory gives exit 1. Its source appends every rule hit to one list and returns 1 if the list is non-empty, so it is also a third checker with no severity control.

findings.title: M1-S02's deploy-order input names two manual steps; two of its own tests read five out of that file
findings.detail: inputs.deploy_order still says the note carries 'the two steps no deploy performs', while this step's manual clauses (e) and (f) ask a reviewer to read the D14 assignee union and the A5 confirmation flag out of deploy-order.md, and M1-S05's list has grown to five. The instruction that tells the builder what to write is narrower than the tests that read it. Warning rather than blocker: it is prose, the mismatch surfaces at the M1 gate rather than in a deployed artefact, and amend-step --prose-only is a documented writer for exactly this once the build is building.

findings.title: M1-S04's new test description credits the checker with a rule that cannot fire on this build
findings.detail: The description says the checker 'fails on rollback-unsafe logging'. Rule 2's pattern is name-bound - 'insert new Error_Log__c(' or an insert of an identifier matching error/log - so DML on this build's Integration_Failure__c never trips it. What the checker actually adds to M1-S04 is the empty-directory guard plus rules 1, 3, 4, 5 and the generic-catch rule, which is the live constraint on this step's code: a catch (Exception e) followed only by System.debug or a silent return exits 1.

findings.title: Three of ten checkers have no severity control, and seven of ten pass on an empty directory
findings.detail: check_object_creation_and_design.py, check_platform_events_apex.py and now check_error_handling_framework.py each fail on findings their own text calls advisory, and only three of the ten declared checkers exit 1 on an empty tree. Which steps can fail on an absent artefact therefore remains an accident of which checkers a step cites - PV-003 was that accident landing badly. A fourth argument form also surfaced this round: check_apex_hardcoded_id_elimination.py takes --src, beyond the three the section 5 follow-up note enumerates, which is why M1-S03 cites that skill without declaring its checker.
